title: Finiteness and finiteness of the quotient by the integral closure for a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the three properties of the integral closure A' of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring A that make the delta-invariant well defined: A' is a normal Nagata ring, A -> A' is finite, and the quotient A'/A has finite length as an A-module. The finiteness of A -> A' is the Nagata hypothesis, and the length statement is obtained by choosing an element f of the maximal ideal satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding lemma, so that A_f equals A'_f; hence the support of the finite module A'/A is contained in the maximal ideal, and the module has finite length by the support-point lemma (proof lines 8301-8315). H2: the reduction of the length statement to the support of A'/A and the use of the element f are the substance, and the argument is short but complete.
